page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dpdsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an ARM64-based Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The instance features 32 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, providing a total of 32 vCPUs. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 128 MB of shared L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core.

For local storage, the server includes a bundled 1890 GB NVMe SSD and supports Premium Storage. In benchmark testing, the hardware demonstrates strong multi-core performance, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory performance is particularly notable, with large-block memory read and write bandwidths ranking in the top 10% tier. This memory efficiency is reflected in PassMark database operations and memory scores, which also place in the top 10% tier.

While multi-threaded execution and memory throughput are highly efficient, single-core performance remains in the average tier, as seen in stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core tests. Additionally, large-model LLM inference prompt processing represents a performance bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 10% tier. Given these characteristics, the D32pds_v6 is highly suited for multi-threaded workloads, database operations, static web serving, and memory-intensive general-purpose applications that benefit from local NVMe storage and high memory bandwidth.
